title: Pieter Maertensz. Coy (Dutch agent in Morocco), 25-sign cipher alphabet with name-numerals, sent to the States General with his letter of 18 Mar 1606 (P.S. 21 Apr)
where: Printed in H. de Castries, Les sources inedites de l'histoire du Maroc, 1re serie, Pays-Bas, letter XXXV, pp. 133-137 (the editor describes the key: 25 conventional signs for the letters of the alphabet plus numerals: Roi du Maroc 2, Roi de Fez 3, Roi de Sous 4, ...). Dutch original text at the foot of the same pages. Archive.org: https://archive.org/details/lessourcesindit02castgoog (OCR https://archive.org/download/lessourcesindit02castgoog/lessourcesindit02castgoog_djvu.txt, line about 9680 of the OCR)
ciphertext: none found. The editor writes (same volume, note to a later letter, OCR line about 12395) that Coy's cipher correspondence 'n'existe plus au Rijksarchief', so the ciphered letters sent after 1606 are lost or unlocated. Candidates for a rediscovery: Staten-Generaal Lias Marokko (Nationaal Archief 1.01.02), which this sweep could not search at item level for Marokko letters (the Secrete kas envoy letters are physical only, see research/nationaal_archief)
use: key for any Coy letter of 1606-07 that turns up; also a bound on what the Dutch Morocco correspondence of the period contained
seen: catalogue (printed edition, OCR text only; the key signs themselves were not looked at on the page image)

title: Key to a secret script, 'probably of Van de Spiegel', with a covering letter of 19 Oct 1927 from N.J. Nederburgh-Prins to Cornelis Bastiaan Nederburgh
kind: key only (the key itself is older)
where: Nationaal Archief, 1.10.59 (S.C. Nederburgh and family), inv. 1578. Found by item search 'geheimschrift' and 'sleutel'. The fonds is that of S.C. Nederburgh (Commissioner-General for the Asian possessions, he visited the Cape in 1793: not checked in this sweep whether the key concerns Cape business)
ciphertext: none in the item as described. DECODE holds 14 Van de Spiegel records (see research/nationaal_archief README); this key may bear on them. Scan status not checked
use: possible key for the Van de Spiegel number code (L.P. van de Spiegel, Raadpensionaris 1787-95)

title: Stukken over het aan Elout en Van Grasveld medegegeven cijfer (papers on the cipher given to Elout and Van Grasveld)
where: Nationaal Archief 2.01.27.02 (Raad der Aziatische Bezittingen en Etablissementen 1800-1806), inv. V.B.317. Same archive, III.B.e inv. 209: draft secret missive of the Council to the Council of the Indies (C.J. Prediger, Batavia), with an 'overbrenging in cijfer' (the text put into cipher) and a later post-scriptum, added to a triplicate sent 20 Apr 1801
ciphertext: inv. 209 holds a ciphered rendering; not scanned (availability not checked). Batavia, not Africa; recorded because it is a colonial-council cipher found by the Africa terms
use: Bataafsche Republiek colonial cipher; link to the Cape not checked
